overview.headline: A steady week. A smaller next plan.
overview.summary: Protect the next dated deadline, allow room for similar tasks that took longer than estimated, and make the next plan fit the entered availability.

findings.observation: Saved study was 420 minutes against a stable 480-minute target. The original task plan has six of eight tasks completed.
findings.interpretation: The next week has less entered availability than this week. Reusing the old target would create a commitment that does not fit the supplied windows.
findings.uncertainty: A time shortfall does not establish its cause or prove less learning. The next-week time commitment is a user choice, not an AI-set goal.
findings.recommendation: Review the old target alongside the candidate plan: it commits 255 study minutes and keeps 45 minutes unallocated. Confirm a realistic new target before saving.
findings.check_next_week: At the next review, compare recorded study with the target the user actually accepted, and show any changes made during the week.

findings.observation: Maths has 270 recorded minutes and Biology 150. The next dated exam is Biology on 20 November; three selected Biology tasks need an estimated 135 minutes.
findings.interpretation: Subject time does not need to be equal. The imminent entered deadline provides a concrete reason to protect the selected Biology work first.
findings.uncertainty: The report cannot know whether those tasks cover the entire exam syllabus or whether Biology is a weak subject.
findings.recommendation: Keep B4, B5 and B6 in the candidate plan before the exam date; review the lower-priority Maths work for deferral.
findings.check_next_week: Check whether B4, B5 and B6 were completed before the entered exam date; do not convert that status into an exam-readiness score.

findings.observation: Three completed, linked Maths tasks have 90 initial estimated minutes and 135 recorded lifetime minutes through cutoff: 45 minutes more, or 50%.
findings.interpretation: For this sample, an average 30-minute estimate corresponded to 45 recorded minutes. Similar next tasks may need a larger estimate or smaller scope.
findings.uncertainty: Only three matched tasks are represented. Missing estimates and unfinished tasks are excluded; this is not a 50% prediction for all future Maths work.
findings.recommendation: For the next comparable practice task, try an editable 40-50 minute estimate or two smaller parts. Check remaining work after the first part.
findings.check_next_week: Compare the next dated, completed task with its original estimate and recorded effort, keeping the same matching rules.

findings.observation: The candidate task list requires 420 minutes. The five entered weekday windows provide 300 study minutes after breaks.
findings.interpretation: The list exceeds capacity by 120 minutes even before keeping any buffer. The selected candidate keeps 255 minutes of priorities and 45 minutes unallocated.
findings.uncertainty: Remaining work is user-estimated. The exam has a date but no start time, so the candidate does not assume exam-day Biology preparation capacity.
findings.recommendation: Defer the optional M6 and M7 tasks, releasing 165 minutes while preserving them in the task list. Review the candidate rather than adding unavailable time.
findings.check_next_week: Check whether the accepted priorities and buffer were workable, and refresh the draft if availability or remaining work changed.

findings.observation: Of two explicitly accepted previous actions, A1 links to completed task M3 and A2 to open task B4 with 45 estimated minutes remaining.
findings.interpretation: The completed action should not be proposed as new work. The unfinished linked task is a concrete candidate for the next plan.
findings.uncertainty: Accepted action status does not show that advice caused a learning improvement. Unlinked tasks must not be counted as followed advice.
findings.recommendation: Carry B4 into Monday while preserving its existing task identity and recorded work; do not recreate M3.
findings.check_next_week: At the next report, inspect the dated completion or updated remaining-work feedback for B4.

findings.observation: Four complete-week saved-time totals are 240, 300, 420 and 420 minutes under the same scope.
findings.interpretation: Recorded time rose and then stayed level. The next decision should account for deadlines and task completion rather than aim for a longer bar by default.
findings.uncertainty: A flat time total is not evidence of stalled understanding. These figures do not identify a cause or an optimal study duration.
findings.recommendation: Keep the manageable rhythm if it suits the user; review the smaller next-week commitment against the time actually available.
findings.check_next_week: Review the same-scope time trend together with dated completion and estimate accuracy, not as a standalone learning-quality score.

next_plan.explanation: Keep the three Biology preparation tasks before the exam date, then retain the two selected Maths priorities. Reserve buffer instead of filling every available study minute.
tradeoffs: M6 optional practice and M7 note rewriting are deferred, not deleted.
The previous weekly target needs separate review; accepting a task plan does not silently change the target.
fallbacks: If priority work remains after Wednesday, review Thursday before adding unavailable time.
Refresh the draft if the entered availability, task status or remaining-work estimates change.

unknowns: Exam start time was not provided.
Remaining work is estimated, not guaranteed.
The records do not measure grades, attention or mastery.
